q: 1. Igneous rock has .....
options: foliated structure which is hard and durable
layers of different composition, colour and structure
explain: Igneous rocks form by cooling and solidification of molten magma, giving a crystalline, glassy or fused texture. Foliated structure belongs to metamorphic rocks and layered structure to sedimentary rocks.

q: 2. Gneiss is chemically classified as .....
explain: Gneiss is rich in silica (quartz and feldspar, like granite), so chemically it is a silicious rock. Geologically it is metamorphic.

q: 3. Marble is an example of .....
explain: Marble is formed when limestone is altered by heat and pressure, so it is a metamorphic rock.

q: 4. The curved swellings from the growth of layers or wounds left after branches are cut off in an irregular manner are known as .....
explain: Rind galls are curved swellings formed where the growth of layers over wounds (left by branches cut off irregularly) takes place.

q: 5. The burning of bricks in kilns is complete within ..... hours.
explain: As per the answer key, burning in kilns is completed in about 24 hours.

q: 6. The bricks after burning in kilns require about ..... days to cool down for unloading.
explain: As per the answer key, bricks need about 12 days to cool down in the kiln before unloading.

q: 7. The bricks should be burnt at temperature from .....
explain: Good bricks are burnt at 1000°C to 1200°C so that the clay vitrifies and gains strength.

q: 8. The type of brick suitable for panel walls for multi-storeyed buildings is .....
explain: Hollow and perforated bricks are light, which reduces dead load on the frame, so both suit panel (non-load-bearing) walls.

q: 9. The compressive strength of perforated bricks should not be less than .....
explain: As per the answer key, the minimum compressive strength of perforated bricks is 7 MN/m².

q: 10. The compressive strength of paving bricks should not be less than .....
explain: Paving bricks must resist heavy wear and load, so the minimum compressive strength is 40 MN/m² as per the answer key.

q: 11. The length of a curved tile varies from .....
explain: As per the answer key, the length of a curved tile ranges from 15 to 20 cm.

q: 12. The dolomite bricks are .....
explain: Dolomite (calcium-magnesium carbonate) is basic in nature, so dolomite bricks are basic refractory bricks used in basic furnace linings.

q: 13. Quick lime is a .....
options: product left immediately after the calcinations of pure limestone
explain: Quick lime is the product left immediately after calcination of limestone. Although chemically it is CaO, the answer key gives option c.

q: 14. After the addition of water to it, the cement sets and hardens due to .....
options: the heat produced by the chemical action
the hydration and hydrolysis of the constituent compounds of cement
explain: Cement sets and hardens by hydration and hydrolysis of its compounds (C3S, C2S, C3A, C4AF), forming a rigid gel.

q: 15. The consistency test is performed to find .....
explain: The consistency test (Vicat) finds the water percentage that gives a paste of standard consistency, used for setting time and soundness tests.

q: 16. For normal consistency, the penetration in Vicat apparatus should be between .....
explain: Standard consistency is reached when the plunger stops 5 to 7 mm from the bottom, i.e. penetrates about 33 to 35 mm of the 40 mm mould.

q: 17. In briquette test, the seven day tensile strength of good Portland cement should not be less than .....
explain: The seven-day tensile strength of a good Portland cement briquette should be at least 25 kg/cm².

q: 18. The seven day compressive strength of a good Portland cement, as obtained from the compressive test on cement-sand mortar cubes, should not be less than .....
explain: The seven-day compressive strength of cement-sand mortar cubes should be at least 175 kg/cm² (about 17.5 MPa).

q: 19. The final setting time of ordinary Portland cement should not be less than .....
explain: As per the answer key, option c (10 h). Note: the usual code limit is that final setting time should not be MORE than 10 hours, so this question is worded oddly in the book.

q: 20. Quick setting cement is used .....
options: for the construction of structures under water
where resistance to acidic water is required
explain: Quick setting cement sets fast, so it is used for underwater work and in running water where the cement must set before being washed away.

q: 21. The initial and final setting times of quick setting cement are .....
explain: Quick setting cement has an initial setting time of about 5 minutes and a final setting time of about 30 minutes.

q: 22. The pozzolona portland cement gains the strength .....
options: in the same time as ordinary Portland cement
in less time than ordinary Portland cement
In more time than ordinary Portland cement
explain: Pozzolanic reaction with lime is slow, so pozzolana Portland cement gains strength more slowly than ordinary Portland cement.

q: 23. Compared to the ordinary Portland cement, the ultimate strength of the pozzolona Portland cement is .....
explain: Although early strength is lower, the continued pozzolanic reaction gives pozzolana cement a higher ultimate strength.

q: 24. In low heat cement, the proportion of the following compound is kept at low value .....
explain: C3A and C3S liberate most of the heat of hydration, so both are kept low in low heat cement.

q: 25. In the chemical composition test for loss on ignition, the cement is heated to a temperature of .....
explain: In the loss on ignition test the cement sample is ignited at about 1000°C to drive off moisture and CO2.

q: 26. Loss on ignition in cement should not exceed .....
explain: Loss on ignition indicates moisture and CO2 absorbed during storage; it should not exceed 4%.

q: 27. The insoluble residues in good cement should be .....
explain: As per the answer key, the insoluble residue in good cement should be less than 1.5%.

q: 28. Excessive free lime and excessive magnesia present in the cement make the cement .....
options: to have very low initial setting time
to have very low compressive strength
explain: Free lime and magnesia hydrate slowly after setting and expand, causing cracks and disintegration; such cement is unsound.

q: 29. Snowcem is .....
explain: Snowcem is a proprietary cement-based paint (coloured cement) used for exterior wall finishing. It is the closest option here.

q: 30. Bitumen felt is used for .....
explain: Bitumen felt is used both as a water-proofing layer (roofs) and as a damp-proof course.

q: 31. The operation of removal of impurities or clay adhering to iron ores, is known as .....
explain: Dressing (or concentration) removes clay and other impurities adhering to the ore by washing or crushing before further treatment.

q: 32. If the iron ore contains clay as an impurity, the flux added during calcinations is .....
explain: Clay is acidic, so a basic flux such as limestone is added to combine with it and form slag.

q: 33. Pit iron made from haematite ores free from sulphur, phosphorus and copper, is known as .....
explain: Bessemer pig iron is made from pure haematite ores free from sulphur, phosphorus and copper.

q: 34. Pig iron obtained from the furnace which is properly provided with fuel at a very high temperature, is called .....
explain: With plenty of fuel and high temperature, carbon separates as graphite, giving grey (foundry) pig iron.

q: 35. If the furnace is provided with insufficient fuel at low temperatures, the type of pig iron produced, is called .....
explain: Insufficient fuel and low temperature keep carbon combined, giving white (forge) pig iron.

q: 36. The variety of pig iron used for the manufacture of steel by Bessemer process, is .....
explain: Bessemer pig iron, being low in sulphur and phosphorus, is used in the Bessemer process.

q: 37. First class timber has an average life of .....
explain: First class timber (like teak) is durable and has an average life of more than 10 years.

q: 38. Refractory bricks are used for .....
explain: Refractory bricks withstand very high temperatures, so they line furnaces and combustion chambers.

q: 39. The fire clay contains pure .....
explain: Fire clay consists mainly of hydrated aluminium silicate (alumina and silica), which gives it high heat resistance.

q: 40. Refractory bricks are .....
explain: Refractory bricks are classified as acid, basic and neutral types, so all the options are correct.

q: 41. Sewer pipes are made of .....
explain: Stoneware is hard, glazed and impervious, so it is used for sewer and drain pipes.

q: 42. Duco paints are .....
explain: Duco is a trade name for nitro-cellulose lacquer paint, i.e. a cellulose paint.

q: 43. Bituminous fells are used for .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: bitumen felts are commonly used for roof water-proofing and D.P.C. as well, so this question is ambiguous in the book.

q: 44. Dry rot .....
explain: Dry rot, caused by fungus, reduces timber to a dry powder.

q: 45. In paints, the pigment is responsible for .....
explain: Pigments give the paint its colour (and opacity).

q: 46. The percentage of alumina and silica in good fire clay vary respectively is .....
explain: As per the answer key, good fire clay has about 25 to 30% alumina and 70 to 75% silica; option a matches.

q: 47. For slaking of 10 kg of CaO, the theoretical amount of water is .....
explain: CaO + H2O gives Ca(OH)2. Molar masses are 56 and 18, so water needed = 10 × 18/56 ≈ 3.2 kg.

q: 48. Pick up the compound responsible for early strength of cement from the following .....
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) hydrates quickly and gives the early strength (up to about 7 days). C3A causes flash set but contributes little strength.

q: 49. The percentage of the residue left after sieving good Portland cement in 90 micron sieve should not exceed .....
explain: For fineness, the residue on a 90 micron IS sieve should not exceed 10%.

q: 50. The expansion in portland cement can be tested by .....
explain: The soundness test (Le Chatelier apparatus or autoclave) measures expansion due to free lime and magnesia.

q: 51. The compressive strength of a good Portland cement and standards and mortar after 3 days of curing should not be less than .....
explain: As per the older IS, the 3-day compressive strength of standard mortar should not be less than 11.5 MN/m².

q: 52. The sand is mixed with lime mortar to .....
explain: Sand is an inert filler that reduces shrinkage and cracking of lime mortar and makes it porous so CO2 can reach it.

q: 53. Into how many units are all the rocks geologically classified?
explain: Geologically, rocks are classified into three groups: igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic.

q: 54. Which of the following rocks is used in cement manufacturing?
explain: Limestone supplies the calcium oxide (lime) which is the main raw material for cement.

q: 55. Plywood is normally available .....
explain: As per the answer key, option d. Note: this thickness refers to a plywood sheet of the given range in the book.

q: 56. Plywood is made from .....
explain: As per the answer key, option c. Note: plywood is normally made from thin veneers of various woods, so this key answer looks doubtful.

q: 57. Fibre boards can be .....
explain: As per the answer key, option d. Note: fibre boards can also be painted and distempered, so the question is ambiguous in the book.

q: 58. The most commonly used base for timber painting, is .....
explain: White lead is the most common base for painting woodwork.

q: 59. The commonly used base for iron and steel work, is .....
explain: Red lead has anti-corrosive properties and is used as the base (primer) for iron and steel.

q: 60. A volatile substance added to a paint to make its application easy and smooth, is known as .....
explain: A solvent (thinner) is volatile and evaporates after application, making the paint easy to spread.

q: 61. Most commonly used solvent in oil paints, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: turpentine is also very widely used as a thinner in oil paints, so this key answer is debatable.

q: 62. Turpentine oil is used in paints as .....
explain: Turpentine is a volatile liquid used as a thinner, which evaporates after the paint is applied.

q: 63. Linseed oil is used in paints as .....
explain: Linseed oil is a drying oil that acts as the vehicle (carrier) for pigment, forming a film when it dries.

q: 64. Varnish is a transparent or semi-transparent solution of resinous substances in .....
explain: Varnish can be made by dissolving resins in alcohol (spirit varnish), linseed oil (oil varnish) or turpentine (turpentine varnish).

q: 65. A bull nose brick is not used for .....
explain: Bull nose bricks have rounded edges for corners, pillars and decoration; arches use wedge-shaped (voussoir) bricks.

q: 66. Second class bricks .....
options: produce a metallic sound when struck
explain: As per the answer key, option b. Note: a metallic ringing sound is more typical of first class bricks, so this key answer is doubtful.

q: 67. Jhumb bricks are .....
explain: Jhamb (jhumb) bricks are over-burnt bricks that are irregular and vitrified.

q: 68. The portion of the brick cut across its width and having its length equal to that of a full brick, is known as .....
explain: As per the answer key, option b (queen closer).

q: 69. The cracks which extend from bark towards the sap wood in the cross section of a tree, are called .....
explain: As per the answer key, option b (star shakes): cracks radiating from the bark inwards, wider at the circumference.

q: 70. The cracks caused by shrinkage of the exterior surface of the wood exposed to atmosphere are called .....
explain: As per the answer key, option c. Shrinkage of the outer surface on exposure to the atmosphere causes surface cracks (wind cracks).
